cases.exposure_context_quote: Case A: A 13-year-old, previously healthy Chinese girl was sent to a local hospital 1 h after ingesting DQ.
cases.agent: diquat (liquid formulation, 200 g/L), about 15 mL, alimentary canal, oral/swallow
cases.circumstance: accidental/consumed pesticide found; circumstance beyond 'was found to have consumed the pesticide' UNVERIFIED

symptoms.finding: >10 episodes of emesis (pale yellow vomitus with pungent taste)
symptoms.quote: Two hours later, the patient had experienced > 10 episodes of emesis, producing pale yellow vomitus with a pungent taste.

symptoms.finding: persistent burning upper abdominal pain and palpitations
symptoms.quote: Two hours later, she exhibited persistent burning upper abdominal pain and palpitations.

symptoms.finding: erythematous posterior pharynx (no drooling or respiratory symptoms)
symptoms.quote: She did not exhibit any drooling or respiratory symptoms, but the posterior pharynx was erythematous.

symptoms.finding: burning sensation in oropharynx; nausea/vomit; abdominalgia/diarrhea; oropharyngeal/esophageal ulcer

cases.time_to_care: sent to local hospital 1 h after ingestion; transferred to Lanzhou University Second Hospital PICU 8 h after ingesting DQ

labs.name: erosive esophagitis and superficial gastritis with bile reflux (gastroscopy day 4)
labs.quote: Gastroscopy results on the fourth day of admission revealed erosive esophagitis and superficial gastritis with bile reflux.

treatment.name: gastric lavage (1 h after poisoning)
treatment.quote: After receiving a gastric lavage, she was transferred to Lanzhou University Second Hospital pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) 8 h after ingesting DQ.

treatment.name: continuous blood purification (CBP, hemoperfusion, model HA320) starting 8 h after poisoning, 3 sessions
treatment.quote: CBP√√CBP times36Interval time(h)Poisoning and first gastric lavage1 h after6 h afterPoisoning and first CBP8 h after90 h after

treatment.name: diuretic, omeprazole, Vitamin C, glutathione; no glucocorticoid/antibiotic/mecobalamin/adsorbent/drainage

cases.sequelae: no obvious pulmonary or laboratory abnormalities attributable to DQ (early hemoperfusion); long-term follow-up stated as required
cases.notes: Diquat ingestion ~15 mL of 200 g/L liquid. No imaging abnormalities (chest radiograph day 1 no obvious abnormalities).

cases.circumstance: accidental/consumed pesticide found; circumstance beyond 'was found to have consumed the pesticide' UNVERIFIED

symptoms.quote: She had experienced nausea and vomiting, producing pale yellow vomitus with a pungent taste.
She was flushed and experiencing chest tightness and an epigastric pain.
